column47: The Department of African Cultural Studies at the University of Wisconsin–Madison provides students with a site for the intensive study of African languages and expressive cultures. Our program is unique in its focus on the intersection of three major areas: linguistics, literature, and culture. We offer a Master of Arts and a Doctor of Philosophy. Students are expected to engage with all three areas, while specializing in one. The department is also known for its strong emphasis on language pedagogy and its commitment to the study of African languages as a key to understanding African cultures. The M.A. degree may be a finishing degree for students who wish to use their expertise in African cultural studies for careers in government, non-governmental organizations, or the private sector. It may also be a step toward the Ph.D. degree.

column47: The Department of African Cultural Studies provides undergraduate and graduate students with a holistic understanding of African expressive cultures. Our faculty and students study the languages, literatures, and other cultural forms of Africa and the African diaspora. Our curriculum includes courses in over a dozen African languages and in the literatures and cultures of Africa and its diaspora. We take a wide-ranging approach to the study of the continent and its people, looking at both traditional and contemporary forms of expression. We are a community of scholars and students who are passionate about the study of Africa and its people. Our program is designed to provide students with a deep and nuanced understanding of African cultures, as well as the skills they need to pursue careers in a variety of fields, including academia, international development, journalism, and more. The Ph.D. program in African Cultural Studies is designed for students who wish to pursue advanced research in the field. Students work closely with faculty members to develop their own research projects, and they have the opportunity to participate in a variety of research seminars and workshops.

column47: Agronomy is the study of plant-soil-climate interactions. The Department of Agronomy at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is home to internationally recognized faculty, many of whom have won major campus and professional honors. Faculty interests range from molecular biological studies of plant growth to ecological studies of agroecosystems. Research and teaching within the department emphasize two major areas: plant breeding and plant genetics; and crop physiology, production, and management. Within these areas, faculty specialize in such fields as sustainable agriculture, international agriculture, weed science, and biotechnology. Students are prepared for careers in agribusiness, crop consulting, university teaching and research, and state and federal agencies. column47:
The Department of Astronomy offers a Ph.D. in astronomy and a M.S. in astronomy. The M.S. is primarily for students pursuing a Ph.D. in astronomy or a related field; students are not normally admitted for a terminal M.S. degree. Research is carried out in both observational and theoretical areas. Current observational research includes the interstellar medium, stellar atmospheres, white dwarf stars, binary stars, star formation, galactic structure, local group galaxies, and observational cosmology. Theoretical research includes star formation, solar physics, plasma astrophysics, and cosmology. Students also participate in the development of instrumentation for both ground-based and space-based telescopes.

The Astronomy Department is located on the top floors of Sterling Hall and the adjacent Chamberlin Hall. The department consists of 14 faculty, approximately 25 graduate students, 35 undergraduate students, and 25 research and support staff. The department also has strong ties to the Physics Department, with several members of that department also conducting research in astronomy and astrophysics.

The department is a major partner in the 10-meter Southern African Large Telescope (SALT). Research facilities also include the 3.5-meter WIYN telescope at Kitt Peak, Arizona, and the Washburn Observatory on the UW–Madison campus. Department members have a long history of participation in space astronomy including the Hubble Space Telescope, the Wisconsin Ultraviolet Photo-polarimeter Experiment (WUPPE) which flew twice on the space shuttle, and the development of the High Speed Photometer for Hubble.

Materials science and engineering is a versatile and interdisciplinary field that uses the principles of physics and chemistry to solve real-world problems. Materials scientists and engineers create the materials that make new technologies possible. Faculty and students in MS&E work on a wide range of materials, including metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers, and composites. They also study materials at all scales, from the atomic and molecular level to the macroscopic level. MS&E is a critical field for many industries, including aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and medicine. MS&E graduates are in high demand by employers in both the public and private sectors. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering at UW-Madison is a leading center for MS&E research and education. The department has a world-class faculty, state-of-the-art facilities, and a strong track record of success. MS&E graduates from UW–Madison are well-prepared for careers in academia, industry, and government.

column47: The Department of Integrative Biology (formerly the Department of Zoology) is a leader in research and graduate training in the biological sciences. Our research programs span the range of biological questions from molecules to ecosystems, from the laboratory to the field, and from simple to complex organisms. The breadth of our research is reflected in our training programs. Research in iBio is roughly divided into three areas: Cell, Molecular, and Developmental Biology; Evolution, Systematics, and Genetics; and Ecology, Behavior, and Organismal Biology. Students are encouraged to pursue research within these areas or to explore the connections between them. Our graduate students have a long history of professional success. Our alumni hold faculty positions in many of the nation's leading universities and colleges. Others are leaders in state and federal agencies and in the private sector. The department offers a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) and a Master of Science (M.S.) in Zoology.
